summary: Weekly POC sync focused on regressive failures seen in the scoring heatmap. Team agreed to try an enriched prompt set (context windows + few-shot exemplars), adjust scoring thresholds for the reranker, and run a short hosted vs dedicated throughput bench to validate latency/cost tradeoffs. Security review requested before any Dedicated pilot. Action items assigned for prompt pack, bench, and failure collection.
topics: Recent regression signal and failure modes
Scoring rubric adjustments and false positive threshold
transcript: [00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got a lot to cover today so we'll keep it tight. Priya, you wanna kick off with the high level on the failures you saw this week?

[00:16] Priya (Cobalt - Head ML): Yeah thanks Maya. So our heatmap still shows a cluster around the 'ephemeral-entity' cases — basically hallucination where the model invents product ids. It started after the parameter tweak last sprint, not sure if it's prompt drift or scoring sensitivity

[00:35] Daniel (SE): Can you point to the exact prompt family? is this from the long-context prompts or the short summary ones? sometimes the KV cash hits are different, like KV cache — sorry — kv cache behavior causes token leakage

[00:52] Priya: Mostly the long-context conversation templates. We increased contextLen to 1.8k tokens. We thought adding more context would stabilize but it looks like more spurious anchors show up. examples are in the sheet we shared (benchmarks: coch-bench- V1).

[01:15] Liam (Product): The worrying part is that some of these hallucinations are surfaced to downstream product flows, so we need thresholds that block them before they hit customers. Our okr is <0.1% false positive for flagged sensitive items

[01:33] Maya: Good. Quick note — we pulled the scoring heatmap and saw the same spikes. My read is two-fold: prompt framing plus the reranker threshold. We recommended a prompt enrichment approach — add two few-shot exemplars and a short negative exemplar showing what NOT to do. That often helps the model settle on the right behavior.
[01:55] Sara (Engineer): Quick q — do you mean inlined examples or reference doc? inlining will bump token counts and could affect latency

[02:10] Daniel: Inlined examples but compact. We can do 2 examples, each 2-3 lines. Also we want to try prefix caching — the Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching so repeated context shouldn't re-cost as much. keep in mind caching behavior differs between hosted and Dedicate — Redwood Dedicate sometimes uses a slightly different kernel path so latency numbers can vary.
[02:40] Marcus (Ops): On the Ops side we can't move to Dedicated until we finish a short security review — VPC peering, KMS integration and the SOC2 artifacts. that's blocking for now
[02:55] Ivy (CSM): Noted. We'll get that scheduled. Maya, can you send the security checklist?
[03:05] Maya: Yep I'll send the security one-pager and the SOC2 link after this call. also we'll include a short doc on network options (V-P-C, private link) and KMS flows.

[03:20] Priya: Back to failures — we also noticed the reranker often gives borderline scores of 0.52-0.58 where human labelers flip. maybe the threshold should be 0.65? but that increases false negatives

[03:36] Daniel: The scoring model is calibrated on their original corpus. we can tune the threshold and also add a confidence margin — like if token-level entropies are high, force a conservative fallback to a safer variant. Redwood supports fallback policies by model variant if latency budget allows.
[03:58] Liam: Fallbacks are good but they add complexity. can we quantify cost? eg, p95 latency and token cost delta if we trigger fallback 5% of the time

[04:12] Daniel: We'll run a 48-hour bench for hosted and dedicated with a synthetic traffic pattern that mirrors your production rate. That will give p50/p95 latencies and token unit costs. we'll include fallback-on and fallback-off curves.
[04:28] Priya: perfect. also on the prompt pack, please mark which prompts are intended for reranker vs generator, we've had some conflation in the last upload

[04:40] Maya: will do — annotated pack inbound. one other quick item: we saw a subset of failures where the model copied proprietary identifiers from context and then mutated them. that's a privacy/safety risk, so we should put a guardrail to redact identifiable patterns pre-send and have the model produce a sanitized token when uncertain.
[05:05] Sara: We can add a regex stage before sending to the model; but we want the model to help decide redaction when pattern is ambiguous. Any suggestions?

[05:18] Daniel: Hybrid approach — regex for obvious patterns, model to flag ambiguous ones. use conservative thresholds on ambiguous flags. also keep an audit trail — Redwood Console retains token-level traces per request for the POC, that helps post-hoc analysis.
[05:40] Priya: about traces — are those encrypted in transit and at rest? Marcus needs to know for the compliance team
[05:48] Maya: yes, TLS in transit and optional KMS-managed keys at rest for Dedicated/private deployments. will send the KMS integration doc.
[06:00] Liam: On evaluation, can we add a micro-metric for hallucination severity rather than just binary pass/fail? like severity 1-5 based on how far it deviates from gold
[06:12] Daniel: Absolutely. We'll add a severity bucket to the scorecard and update the heatmap to color by severity. that will help prioritize fixes.

[06:25] Priya: Another small thing — we saw a temporal drift: prompts referencing 'Q2 2026' caused older context tokens to be weighted too heavily. maybe we should add a temporal decay to the context used in prompt construction
[06:40] Daniel: Good catch. We can add a lightweight decay — move older paragraphs to a condensed synopsis to preserve signal but reduce token weight.

[06:52] Maya: Ok let's land on concrete experiments. experiment A: prompt enrichment inline (2 exemplars + negative), reranker threshold bump to 0.65, severity tagging. experiment B: rollback to previous contextLen with prefix condensation + severity tagging. We'll run both on staging.
[07:10] Sara: which experiment do we test first?
[07:14] Priya: Let's do enrichment first, seems lower risk. If enrichment reduces hallucinations without hurting recall we keep it. If not we'll try condensation.

[07:25] Daniel: I'll wire up the bench to gate on both experiments so we can compare over a 48h window. bench will include p95 latency, cost per 1k requests, and hallucination rate per severity bucket.
[07:38] Liam: ok great. any questions on the scoring rubric update? We need the format: numeric threshold, severity buckets, and examples per bucket
[07:48] Maya: We'll put that in the scoring matrix doc — numeric thresholds and representative examples. that doc will be part of the prompt pack.
[08:00] Marcus: Quick ops question: if we move to Dedicated later how disruptive is model rollforward? we don't want big cutovers

[08:10] Daniel: The deployment abstraction keeps same API. Redwood routes can do canary and A/B rollouts. moving to Dedicated is more capacity provisioning then a routing change — minimal client-side disruption.
[08:25] Priya: there was also a small drift where the reranker trained on older labels prefers recall over precision. Is retraining in scope now?
[08:36] Maya: Retraining is heavier; for the POC we prefer thresholding and prompt engineering first. if post-experiments we still see issues we can scope a small re-finetune.
[08:50] Liam: vendor question — do you support structured output schema enforcement? we want JSON schema outputs enforced to avoid malformed fields
[09:00] Daniel: Yes, Redwood supports structured output and guarded decoding with function-calling style constraints and fallback if schema validation fails. that'll reduce downstream parsing errors.
[09:15] Priya: Great. Also tagged some examples in the shared sheet IIIC that show token-level entropies. Daniel, can you pull those into the bench run?
[09:27] Daniel: Yup will ingest those as weighted inputs.
[09:33] Maya: ok, scheduling notes — SE bench by 2026-08-06, prompt pack and scoring rubric by 2026-08-02, security deep-dive week of 2026-08-09. any blockers to those dates?
[09:46] Marcus: Security team is free week of 8/9 but needs the invite this week. we'll need the SOC2 snippet and KMS steps beforehand.
[09:58] Ivy: I'll send the invite and collect the right folks. Maya will you share the SOC2 link after this call?
[10:07] Maya: Yep, right after. Also I'll include a short note about what we need from you to provision Dedicated if and when we go that route.
[10:20] Priya: One last operational ask: when you run the bench, can you keep a sample trace for each failure with the full prompt+response? that makes debugging easier
[10:32] Daniel: We'll keep redacted traces and a mapping to the sample ids. Redaction will remove any live PII per the regex rules we discussed.
[10:44] Liam: sweet. Anything else from the Redwood side?
[10:48] Maya: No, just that we'll prioritize the prompt pack and bench. also we'll add a brief note on fallback cost delta to the bench results so you can make a business decision on thresholds.
[10:58] Sara: For internal tracking, I'll upload the failure examples to the shared bucket and tag them with severity. expect that by 8/5
[11:07] Priya: thanks. sounds like a plan. I'm comfortable with enrichment first then condensation if needed.
[11:15] Maya: Great. Quick recap before we close — action items and dates again, then we'll wrap.

[11:22] Maya: (recap) 1) Maya: annotated prompt pack + scoring rubric - 8/2. 2) Daniel: 48h bench hosted vs dedicated - 8/6. 3) Sara: failure examples - 8/5. 4) Ivy: security invite & checklist - 8/3. Any clarifications?
[11:41] Priya: None from me. Thanks everyone.
[11:46] Liam: Thanks. we'll review the bench results in next sync — same time next week?
[11:52] Maya: Yes, same time. I'll share the invite. Bye all.
[11:57] [meeting ended]
